Once media-map could read the R2 index, the build left those files out of the deployment (they are on R2), but the tags still pointed same-origin, so production served 404s. media-map only kept paths named in code, and these are named in MDX. The tags now use mediaUrl, as does the fly-connectome poster, so all five come from R2. media-map also keeps any file a raw ,

subject: Load article widgets per page; lighter /articles; diagnosable media-map
body:
Every article page downloaded the interactive widgets of all 500+ articles:
the route imports MDX through one template-literal import(), and Next does
not code-split client components imported by a server component, so all
1,112 widgets sat in the route's entry chunk (7.4 MB raw, 2.0 MB gzipped).

A remark plugin (lib/mdx/remark-lazy-widgets.mjs) rewrites each MDX import
of a "use client" module under components/articles/ into a small client
loader (components/mdx/lazy-widget.tsx) that pulls the widget from a
generated registry with React.lazy, one chunk per widget. Static generation
waits for them, so the HTML is unchanged. Route entry: 0.43 MB raw, 0.12 MB
gzipped; an article page now loads about 0.8 MB raw of JS instead of 7-8 MB.
The registry is regenerated before dev and build; validate:widgets fails
when the committed one is stale.

/articles sends each description cut to its opening sentences (search is
its only reader): 2.80 MB to 2.56 MB of HTML.

media-map's index fetch now names itself, retries, and logs the status and
any Cloudflare cf-mitigated header, so a blocked fetch is visible in the
build log instead of silently serving every file from Vercel.

subject: Run the proxy only where it changes the response
body:
proxy.ts matched every path, so every page view and every CDN cache hit
invoked a function just to attach the RFC 8288 Link header. On Vercel that
is Fast Origin Transfer, and it exhausted the Hobby allowance.

The Link header moves to a next.config.ts route header, applied by the CDN.
The proxy now runs only for /api/*, for clients that name a markdown type
in Accept, and for non-browser clients on paths outside the known routes
(the markdown 404). Browser and crawler page views never reach it.
Verified: the compiled matchers route sample requests as intended, and
check:agents passes 56/56 against next start.
